chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Sabbah who said:

I bear witness that I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I testify that Ali is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that al-Hasan is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that al-Husayn is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that Ali ibn al-Husayn is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory; and that Muhammad ibn Ali is an Imam whose obedience God has made obligatory.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness / I testify — the formal attestation formula, invoking the weight of legal testimony
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: Imam — the divinely appointed leader of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.فَرَضَ اللَّهُ طَاعَتَهُ: God made his obedience obligatory — a formula affirming the divine mandate of each Imam's authority

ai.seo_question: Which hadiths in al-Kafi affirm that obedience to the Imams is divinely obligatory?
ai.summary: Abu al-Sabbah, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), personally testifies that he heard the Imam formally declare the divinely-ordained imamate and obligatory obedience of five successive Imams: Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn (al-Sajjad), and Muhammad ibn Ali (al-Baqir). This hadith establishes the imamate through the framework of divine obligation (fard), where God Himself has imposed the duty of obedience to each Imam. For early Shia audiences, this solemn first-person testimony — using the shahada formula — served as a strong legal and theological attestation of the doctrine of imamate.
